title: Your Lights Just Got Steadier: Government Boosts Energy Storage with ₹14,500 Crore Fund
description: The Indian government has approved a ₹14,500 crore fund to build large-scale energy storage systems. This money, called Viability Gap Funding (VGF), helps pri.

faq.a: VGF is a one-time grant provided by the government to support infrastructure projects that are economically justified but may not be financially attractive to private investors on their own. It helps cover a portion of the project cost to make it commercially viable.

faq.q: What are Grid-Scale Energy Storage Systems?
faq.a: These are large facilities designed to store electricity from the power grid and release it back when needed. They help balance electricity supply and demand, especially with intermittent renewable energy sources.

faq.q: How will this scheme help renewable energy?
faq.a: By providing storage, this scheme allows renewable energy generated during off-peak times (like abundant solar power at noon) to be saved and used during peak demand or when renewable generation is low (like at night). This makes renewable energy a more reliable, "round-the-clock" power source.

faq.q: Will my electricity bill go down immediately?
faq.a: While the long-term goal is to provide more affordable electricity by integrating cheaper renewable sources, immediate changes to your bill might not be seen. The benefits will likely appear gradually as more storage capacity comes online and the energy mix shifts.

faq.q: What does "mandatory domestic content requirement" mean?
faq.a: It means that for certain components or parts of the energy storage systems, especially Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), a specific percentage must be sourced or manufactured within India. This aims to boost local industries and reduce reliance on imports.
